observations.attempt: Coordinator's explicit probe: does the added 'repoId' in message guard change which messages the workspace client acts on, and can it cause the client to act on a message intended for a different repo, or accept a chat-channel 'subscribed' ack as a repo-subscription confirmation? Read parseGatewayMessage end to end (Phase A cold model: what values can actually reach line 62) before accepting review.md's or the coordinator's own characterization of it, then verified against the current shared-types union and a live tsc/test run.
evidence: apps/web/app/workspace/realtime.ts:32-34 -- for `value.type === 'subscribed'`, parseGatewayMessage ALWAYS calls `stringField(value, 'repoId')` and returns `null` when absent, else `{ type: 'subscribed', repoId }`. There is no branch anywhere in this function that reads `value.channel` or constructs a `{ type: 'subscribed', channel: 'chat', conversationId }` literal. Read directly, not inferred: the raw JSON's `channel`/`conversationId` fields, if present, are never even looked at for this `type`. This means `parseGatewayMessage` is structurally incapable today of returning the chat 'subscribed' variant -- confirming review.md's claim rather than merely accepting it.

Because of the above, the ONLY way `message.type === 'subscribed'` is true at realtime.tsx:62 is via the repo variant, which always carries `repoId` (parseGatewayMessage's own null-return guard already excludes the alternative of a repoId-less object reaching this line). So `'repoId' in message` evaluates to `true` on every code path currently reachable at runtime -- it is a runtime no-op today, exactly as claimed, and is load-bearing only for `tsc`'s static narrowing over the now-two-variant `GatewayToClientMessage['subscribed']` union (packages/shared-types/src/index.ts:289,292).

Forward-looking structural check (not merely 'it happens to work today'): even if `parseGatewayMessage` were later widened to decode the chat variant too (which would require an entirely separate code change to this file, itself a sibling-sweep-detectable event), the guard as written would correctly gate the subsequent `.repoId` access and equality comparison to fire only for the repo variant -- 'repoId' in message is false for `{type:'subscribed', channel:'chat', conversationId}` (no repoId key), so a chat-channel ack could never be misread as a repo-subscription confirmation through this line even in that hypothetical future state. This makes the guard correct-by-construction against the coordinator's exact hypothetical, not merely correct against today's parser.

`message.repoId === repositoryId` (unchanged) is still evaluated after the new conjunct, so even the (currently unreachable) case of a same-shaped-but-wrong-repo confirmation is still rejected on the existing equality check -- the new conjunct narrows what CAN reach that comparison, it does not replace or weaken it.

observations.attempt: Coordinator's explicit probe: confirm the guard does not weaken the existing `message.repoId === repositoryId` tenant/repo scoping check that follows it. Compared the exact boolean expression before and after the hand-edit rather than trusting the characterization in changes.md/review.md.
evidence: Before: `message.type === 'subscribed' && message.repoId === repositoryId`. After: `message.type === 'subscribed' && 'repoId' in message && message.repoId === repositoryId`. This is a logical AND of a strictly ADDITIONAL condition ('repoId' in message) ahead of the pre-existing, byte-identical `message.repoId === repositoryId` conjunct -- the diff (`git diff apps/web/app/workspace/state/realtime.tsx`, re-run this session) shows the equality check itself was not touched, reordered, negated, or loosened in any way. A logical AND with an extra conjunct can only ever narrow the set of inputs that satisfy the whole expression, never widen it -- there is no code path that passes the new, longer condition but would have failed the old, shorter one.

The real security boundary this UI-local check feeds into -- whether this client actually receives ONLY events for repositories/conversations it's authorized to see -- lives entirely server-side (CORE-01/CORE-02/WS-04/WS-05's gateway-side observations above: org-scoped connection identity, matchingChat/matching registry lookups, the per-push RBAC re-filter). This client-side `repositoryId` comparison is a UI-state routing decision (which repo's 'connected' indicator to flip) over data the gateway has already restricted to this connection's own authorized `repoId` subscription; it was never itself the security boundary, so a client-side narrowing of the conditions under which that routing fires cannot create a new authorization bypass in either direction.
